predicted.explanation: The root cause is an uncorrectable ECC error on GPU 6 of node01. The kernel log shows Xid 94 error at PCI:0000:ba:00 (GPU 6) with "Contained: CE User Channel" indicating memory corruption, and the metrics show ecc_vol_uncorr=1 starting from sample 343. This GPU fault caused CUDA errors and collective timeouts across all ranks.

The root cause is an uncorrectable ECC error on node01 GPU 5. The NVRM Xid 94 error shows CE User Channel (0x9) indicating memory corruption, which coincides with the CUDA illegal memory access on rank 5 at the same timestamp. This GPU memory corruption caused the collective operation timeouts and job failure as symptoms.

The job failed due to an uncorrectable ECC error on GPU 0 of node02. The NVRM driver logged Xid 94 indicating a memory error that could not be corrected, which eventually caused the CUDA error and collective timeout across all ranks.

GPU 6 on node01 fell off the PCI bus at 09:47:10, as shown by the RmInitAdapter failure with error code 0x26. This caused the GPU to stop reporting metrics and eventually led to collective operation timeouts when other ranks tried to communicate with it.

GPU 4 on node04 failed to initialize with RmInitAdapter errors (0x26:0x56:1474), indicating the GPU fell off the PCIe bus or became unresponsive. This caused the collective operation timeouts as other ranks waited for this dead GPU.

GPU 0 on node01 fell off the bus, as shown by the NVRM RmInitAdapter failure errors. This caused the GPU to become unresponsive, leading to collective operation timeouts across all ranks when the job tried to continue.

The root cause is an InfiniBand link down event on node03, as shown by the mlx5_core error "ibp108s0: Link down" in kern.log. This network failure would cause collective operation timeouts and job failures across all ranks, which matches the observed symptoms. The transient nature of this event (link went down and recovered quickly) explains why it appears as a warning rather than an error in the training logs.

The root cause is an InfiniBand link down on node04 at 12:30:32, which occurred during the job. This network adapter failure would cause communication breakdowns between GPU ranks, leading to collective-operation timeouts and job failure. The IB link down is a hardware-level fault that explains why the training job could not complete successfully.

GPU 7 on node04 accumulated uncorrectable ECC errors (ecc_vol_uncorr ranging from 0 to 16), while all other GPUs showed zero uncorrectable ECC errors. This indicates a hardware fault in GPU 7's memory that caused the training job to fail or degrade.

The job failed due to an OOM kill event on node01 at 15:56:08, as recorded in the scheduler log. This host memory exhaustion caused the training process to be killed, leading to collective timeouts and job failure across all ranks.

The scheduler detected an OOM kill event on node02 at 18:47:37, which caused the training job to fail. No GPU-specific errors (Xid, ECC) were found in kern.log or metrics, indicating this was a host memory issue rather than a GPU fault. The collective timeouts that followed are symptoms of the initial OOM kill propagating across ranks.

The root cause is an IB link down event on node02 at 18:30:25, which caused communication failures between nodes. This led to collective operation timeouts and eventually the job failure due to OOM kills as processes waited for responses that never came.

The root cause is an InfiniBand link failure on node04. The mlx5_core error shows "Cable error, Power budget exceeded" on port 0000:9c:00.0 (mlx5_3), which caused persistent network connectivity issues leading to NCCL collective operation timeouts and job failure.

The root cause is an InfiniBand cable error on node01 at 09:35:24, showing "Cable error, Power budget exceeded" for mlx5_core port. This hardware-level network fault caused the IB link to fail, leading to NCCL collective operation timeouts and job failure across all ranks.

The root cause was an IB link down on node04 due to a cable error with power budget exceeded (mlx5_core Port module event). This physical network failure caused NCCL collective operations to timeout across all ranks, leading to the job failure. The Xid 13 error on node03 occurred before the job started and is not relevant.

The root cause is an NVLink fatal error detected on link 3 of GPU 1 (PCI:0000:2a:00.0) on node03 at 18:17:22, which occurred during the job. This uncorrectable ECC error caused the GPU to fail, leading to NCCL collective operation timeouts and job failure.

The root cause is an uncorrectable NVLink fatal error on GPU 5 of node02 (PCI:0000:ab:00). The kernel log shows "NVRM: Xid 74" with "NVLink: fatal error detected on link 3", which indicates a hardware-level memory or interconnect error that cannot be corrected. This caused the GPU to fail, leading to subsequent NCCL timeouts and job failure across all ranks.

The root cause is an NVLink fatal error on GPU 3 of node02 (PCI:0000:5d:00), indicated by Xid 74 with "NVLink: fatal error detected on link 3". This caused the GPU to fall off the bus, leading to collective operation timeouts and job failure.

The root cause is a GPU hardware fault on node03's GPU 7 (PCI:0000:db:00). The kernel log shows "NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:db:00): 74, ... NVLink: fatal error detected on link 3", which indicates the GPU fell off the bus. This caused NCCL communication failures and collective operation timeouts across all ranks.

The root cause is storage_full on node01, evidenced by the checkpoint save failing with "Disk quota exceeded" error at 17:53:08. This caused the job to eventually timeout on NCCL collective operations as a secondary symptom. The earlier IB link down was transient and recovered quickly, so it's not the root cause.

The job failed because disk quota was exceeded when saving checkpoints. The checkpoint save on node01 at 15:02:44 failed with "OSError: [Errno 122] Disk quota exceeded", which caused the training job to terminate and led to collective operation timeouts across all nodes.

The InfiniBand link on node03 went down (mlx5_core reported "Link down" for ibp60s0), causing collective operation timeouts across all ranks. This network infrastructure failure disrupted GPU-to-GPU and GPU-to-network communication, leading to the job failure.
